title: Work & study
goal: Talk about jobs, school and university, and say what you can, can't and have to do.
intro: 'Can' in Odia is the helper verb **ପାରିବା** attached to another verb: କହିପାରେ 'can speak'. 'Have to' is *to-me it falls to do*: **ମୋତେ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ** 'I'll have to do it'. With these two patterns you can talk about your working day and your studies.

vocab.note: ଚାକିରି କରିବା 'to have a job, work'.
Female: ଶିକ୍ଷୟିତ୍ରୀ (sikhyôyitri). Pupils say ସାର୍ / ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍.
Joined to the -ଇ form: କରିପାରେ, ଯାଇପାରିବି.

phrases.native: ମୁଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଆଇଟି କମ୍ପାନୀରେ କାମ କରେ।
phrases.roman: muṃ goṭie aiṭi kômpanire kamô kôre.
phrases.en: I work in an IT company.

grammar.title: 'Can': -ଇ + ପାରିବା
grammar.body:
Take the verb stem + **-ଇ** (the 'having done' form: କହି, ଯାଇ, ଖାଇ, କରି) and add the right form of **ପାରିବା**, usually written as one word:

ମୁଁ କହିପାରେ 'I can speak' · ଆପଣ କହିପାରନ୍ତି 'you can speak' · ତୁମେ କହିପାର · ସେ କହିପାରେ
Future (very common for specific occasions): ମୁଁ ଆସିପାରିବି 'I'll be able to come', ଆପଣ ଆସିପାରିବେ?
Negative: କହିପାରେ ନାହିଁ / ଆସିପାରିବି ନାହିଁ.
Past: ମୁଁ ଯାଇପାରିଲି ନାହିଁ 'I couldn't go'.

For learned skills you can also use **ଜାଣିବା** 'know (how)': ସେ ଭଲ ରାନ୍ଧି ଜାଣେ 'she knows how to cook well'.

examples.native: ମୁଁ ଓଡ଼ିଆ ପଢ଼ିପାରେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଲେଖିପାରେ ନାହିଁ।
examples.roman: muṃ Oṛia pôṛhipare, kintu lekhipare nahiṃ.
examples.en: I can read Odia, but I can't write it.
I won't be able to come tomorrow.
He/She knows how to cook well.

grammar.title: 'Have to / must': ମୋତେ … -ବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ
grammar.body:
Obligation uses the **dative** (ମୋତେ, ତୁମକୁ, ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ…) + verb in **-ବାକୁ** + **ପଡ଼ିବା** ('to fall') in the right tense:
ମୋତେ ଯିବାକୁ **ପଡ଼େ** — I (regularly) have to go
ମୋତେ ଯିବାକୁ **ପଡ଼ୁଛି** — I have to go (now)
ମୋତେ ଯିବାକୁ **ପଡ଼ିବ** — I'll have to go
ମୋତେ ଯିବାକୁ **ପଡ଼ିଲା** — I had to go

The verb ପଡ଼ିବା never changes for person — the dative shows who. 'Don't have to' = … ପଡ଼ିବ ନାହିଁ. For a strong 'must', use **ନିଶ୍ଚୟ** + future: ତୁମେ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବ 'you must come'. 'Need to' = -ବା + ଦରକାର: ମୋତେ ଯିବା ଦରକାର.

examples.native: ମୋତେ ସକାଳ ଆଠଟାରେ ଅଫିସ୍ ଯିବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ।
examples.roman: mote sôkaḷô aṭhôṭare ôphis jibaku pôṛe.
examples.en: I have to go to the office at 8 a.m.
Tomorrow I have to sit an exam.

examples.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ଏ ଫର୍ମ ପୂରଣ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ।
examples.roman: apôṇôṅku e phôrm purôṇô kôribaku pôṛibô.
examples.en: You'll have to fill in this form.
You don't have to go to the office on Sundays.

dialogue.title: Working late
dialogue.setting: Sam's colleague Priya invites him for tea after work.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ସାମ୍, ଆଜି ସଞ୍ଜରେ ଆମ ସହ ଚା ପିଇବାକୁ ଆସିପାରିବ?
lines.roman: Sam, aji sôñjôre amô sôhô cha piibaku asiparibô?
lines.en: Sam, can you come for tea with us this evening?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମାଫ କରିବ, ଆଜି ପାରିବି ନାହିଁ। ମୋତେ ସାତଟା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ କାମ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ।
lines.roman: maphô kôribô, aji paribi nahiṃ. mote satôṭa pôrjyôntô kamô kôribaku pôṛibô.
lines.en: Sorry, I can't today. I have to work until seven.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: Why? Do you have a lot of work?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଁ, କାଲି ସକାଳେ ମାଲିକଙ୍କୁ ରିପୋର୍ଟ ଦେବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ।
lines.roman: hôṃ, kali sôkaḷe malikôṅku riporṭ debaku pôṛibô.
lines.en: Yes, I have to give the boss a report tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Thanks. Can you make the charts?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ହଁ, ମୁଁ ଭଲ ଚାର୍ଟ କରିପାରେ। ଦିଅ, ମୁଁ କରିଦେବି।
lines.roman: hôṃ, muṃ bhôlô charṭ kôripare. diô, muṃ kôridebi.
lines.en: Yes, I'm good at charts. Give them here, I'll do them for you.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ହା ହା। କିନ୍ତୁ କାଲି ତୁମକୁ ମୋତେ ଚା ପିଆଇବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ!
lines.roman: ha ha. kintu kali tumôku mote cha piaibaku pôṛibô!
lines.en: Ha ha. But tomorrow you'll have to treat me to tea!

culture: Odisha has a long tradition of learning — Utkal University (1943) and Ravenshaw University in Cuttack (1868) are famous. Bhubaneswar is now an IT and education hub. At school and college, teachers are addressed as **ସାର୍** (sir) and **ମ୍ୟାଡାମ୍** or **ଦିଦି**. Colleagues of similar age move quickly to ତୁମେ, but a boss is always ଆପଣ, often with **-ବାବୁ** or **ସାର୍** after the name.

tip.title: I am a teacher: ମୁଁ ଜଣେ ଶିକ୍ଷକ
tip.body:
- No verb is needed for 'am / is': ମୁଁ ଜଣେ ଶିକ୍ଷକ 'I'm a teacher'.
- **ଜଣେ** = 'a' for a person (ଗୋଟିଏ is for things).
- Ask: ଆପଣ କ'ଣ କାମ **କରନ୍ତି**? (polite) · ତୁମେ କ'ଣ କାମ **କର**? (friend).

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଜଣେ ଇଞ୍ଜିନିୟର, ଆଉ ମୋ ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଓକିଲ।
sentences.roman: muṃ jôṇe iñjiniyôrô, au mo stri okilô.
sentences.en: I'm an engineer, and my wife is a lawyer.
I don't have a job right now.
My son is in fifth grade.
The kids go to school at seven.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଓଡ଼ିଆ ବହି ଓ ଖାତା କେଉଁଠି?
sentences.roman: mo Oṛia bôhi o khata keuṃṭhi?
sentences.en: Where are my Odia book and notebook?

tip.title: Can: -ଇ + ପାରିବା
tip.body:
- Verb stem + **-ଇ**, then **ପାରିବା**, written as one word: କହି + ପାରେ → **କହିପାରେ** 'I can speak'.
- Person endings go on ପାରିବା: ମୁଁ କହିପାରେ · ତୁମେ କହିପାର · ଆପଣ **କହିପାରନ୍ତି**.
- For a particular occasion use the future: ଆସିପାରିବି 'I'll be able to come'. 'Can't' = + ନାହିଁ.

sentences.en: I can speak a little Odia.
Can I help you with anything?

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଆଜି ସ୍କୁଲ୍ ଯାଇପାରିବି ନାହିଁ, ମୋର ଜ୍ୱର।
sentences.roman: muṃ aji skul jaiparibi nahiṃ, morô jwôrô.
sentences.en: I can't go to school today — I've got a fever.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଏବେ ବି ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଲେଖିପାରେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ ebe bi Oṛia lekhipare nahiṃ.

lessons.title: At work
new: ମୁଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଆଇଟି କମ୍ପାନୀରେ କାମ କରେ।

sentences.en: My office is near the station.
The boss isn't in the office today.
The meeting is at ten, in the boss's room.
On Saturdays I have a half day off.

tip.title: Have to: ମୋତେ … -ବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ
tip.body:
- The person goes in the **-କୁ** form: **ମୋତେ**, ତୁମକୁ, ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ.
- Then the verb + **-ବାକୁ**, then **ପଡ଼ିବା**: ମୋତେ ଯିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ 'I'll have to go'.
- ପଡ଼ିବା never changes for the person — only for time: ପଡ଼େ (usually) · ପଡ଼ୁଛି (now) · ପଡ଼ିବ (will) · ପଡ଼ିଲା (had to).

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ଆଜି ଶୀଘ୍ର ଅଫିସ୍ ଯିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ।
sentences.roman: mote aji sighrô ôphis jibaku pôṛibô.
sentences.en: I have to go to the office early today.

sentences.native: ସୋମବାର ମୋର ପରୀକ୍ଷା ଅଛି, ସେଥିପାଇଁ ପଢ଼ିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ୁଛି।
sentences.roman: somôbarô morô pôrikhya ôchhi, sethipaiṃ pôṛhibaku pôṛuchhi.
sentences.en: I have an exam on Monday, so I have to study.

sentences.native: ତୁମକୁ ରବିବାର କାମ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ କି?
sentences.roman: tumôku rôbibarô kamô kôribaku pôṛe ki?
sentences.en: Do you have to work on Sundays?

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ସବୁଦିନ ମାଲିକଙ୍କୁ ଫୋନ କରିବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ।
sentences.roman: mote sôbudinô malikôṅku phonô kôribaku pôṛe.
sentences.en: I have to call the boss every day.

sentences.native: ଗତକାଲି ମୋତେ ଡେରି ଯାଏ ରହିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିଲା।
sentences.roman: gôtôkali mote ḍeri jae rôhibaku pôṛila.
sentences.en: Yesterday I had to stay late.

sentences.native: କାଲି ଛୁଟି, ଅଫିସ୍ ଯିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: kali chhuṭi, ôphis jibaku pôṛibô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Tomorrow's a holiday — I won't have to go to the office.
You'll have to get a ticket.
The exam went well — I'm happy.
